html:
In 1864 Prussia and Austria defeated Denmark and took the duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg, a large part of the Danish state.

Danish nationalists had tried to tie Schleswig more closely to the kingdom, against its German-speaking majority in the south. Bismarck seized the chance. The Danish army fell back to the earthworks at Dybbøl, which fell after a heavy siege on 18 April 1864.

The defeat was a turning point for Denmark. It became a small, mostly Danish-speaking country and stopped dreaming of being a great power. Its people turned to reclaiming heathland and to the folk high schools and cooperatives. North Schleswig voted to return in 1920. The war was a first step to the German unification led by Prussia.
sum: In 1864 Prussia and Austria defeated Denmark and took the duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg, a large part of the Danish state.
